extracted.intended_audience: ECCV 2024 reviewers, area chairs, and program committee members
extracted.subtask_description: Conference reviewer guidelines for evaluating ECCV 2024 submissions and for writing thorough, ethical, and constructive reviews that preserve double-blind integrity and technical quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical soundness and contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should be technically sound and make a contribution to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should seek innovation and meaningful contributions rather than only superior benchmark performance. Acknowledge novel approaches even when empirical validation is limited; focus on whether the work advances knowledge or techniques in computer vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on innovation over benchmark superiority
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek innovation and meaningful contributions, not just benchmark performance superiority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate higher numbers on benchmarks with a meaningful contribution; consider conceptual novelty, new problems, or methods that meaningfully move the field forward even if benchmarks are not clearly superior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review substantive depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews require substantive depth and should not be shallow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide explicitly rejects 'bullet lists with one short sentence per bullet' as insufficient. Provide detailed analysis, reasoning, and evidence to support strengths, weaknesses, and the final recommendation. Feedback should guide authors toward improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat papers fairly regardless of author identity or external context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid imposing unnecessary citation burdens for concurrent arXiv work and refrain from rejecting papers solely for missing comparisons to unpublished preprints. Maintain the same standards irrespective of known author identities and be mindful of perceived impartiality issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not actively discover author identities and maintain confidentiality throughout the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve double-blind integrity by avoiding actions that would unblind submissions. Keep submissions and their contents confidential until publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idea safeguarding and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewed materials (submissions, results, code, supplementary materials) remain proprietary until publication and must not be shared or used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must not share submissions or related artifacts with non-reviewers and must not appropriate or use reviewed ideas in their own work. Treat all submission content as confidential intellectual property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest management
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and act on conflicts of interest, declining review when conflicted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts include institutional affiliations, direct collaboration within three years, advisor-advisee relationships, and other perceived impartiality concerns. If conflicted, decline immediately to preserve fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional conduct and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain courtesy and constructiveness in reviews; avoid sarcasm or belittling language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be professional and helpful. Even strong criticisms should be framed constructively with actionable suggestions rather than personal attacks or dismissive remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow reflection before writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Give yourself time to reflect before composing the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take time to form considered judgments rather than writing immediate, potentially superficial comments. Thoughtful reflection helps produce balanced, accurate, and actionable reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide specific, detailed feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer specific and detailed feedback rather than vague statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain precisely what is strong or weak (e.g., methodological flaws, missing baselines, unclear assumptions) and provide concrete examples or questions authors can address. Detailed feedback is more actionable and useful for Area Chairs and authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground novelty claims in citations and explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Support claims about novelty with concrete citations and clear explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When stating that a contribution is novel, explain why and cite relevant related work. Grounding novelty claims helps Area Chairs and authors assess the true contribution and avoids weak or unsupported assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address writing clarity with targeted suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Point out unclear writing and provide specific suggestions to improve clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify confusing sections, suggest reorganizations or clarifications, and indicate where additional explanation or experiments would help. Help authors improve the presentation as well as the technical content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use third-person language in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to submissions in the third-person (e.g., 'the paper') rather than addressing authors directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using neutral phrasing ('the paper') helps keep reviews impersonal and professional, avoiding defensive responses and maintaining focus on the work rather than the authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer constructive improvement suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide actionable suggestions that authors can use to improve their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than only pointing out faults, recommend specific ways to address weaknesses (e.g., additional experiments, clearer explanations, alternative baselines), while being realistic about what can be accomplished in rebuttal versus revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: arXiv/preprint comparison policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are not obligated to compare against recent preprints on arXiv; missing comparisons to arXiv work alone do not warrant rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance gaps with arXiv-only work are not a valid sole reason for rejection. However, obvious direct inspiration from a preprint should be acknowledged by authors. Avoid punishing authors for not benchmarking against concurrent unpublished work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material scope and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material may support derivations and extended results but must not contain improved method versions or corrected PDFs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use supplementary files for detailed derivations, extra experiments, and extended results. Do not accept supplements that introduce improved method variants or corrections to the main PDF. If clarification is needed, reviewers may request it, but they should not demand substantial new experiments during the rebuttal period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal expectations regarding new experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not require substantial new experiments during the rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During rebuttal, requests should focus on clarification and small additional analyses; demanding large-scale new experiments is inappropriate because authors have limited time and resources to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawn datasets policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of discontinued or withdrawn datasets (e.g., DukeMTMC-ReID) warrants scrutiny but is not automatic grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag such uses to Area Chairs for further consideration. Requesting authors to evaluate on withdrawn datasets violates policy. Treat each case carefully and consult Chairs when data provenance or ethics concerns arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset contribution and release expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper's primary contribution is a dataset, there is a reasonable expectation that the dataset will be publicly released upon publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers claiming dataset contributions should plan for public release; however, the use of non-public datasets for training does not automatically disqualify a submission. Consider practicality, privacy, and ethical constraints when judging dataset papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM / language-model tool usage policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may use LLMs only for 'polishing' review wording; showing submissions to LLMs or using LLMs to generate summaries is misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polishing wording with an LLM is acceptable if the reviewer vouches for the accuracy of content. Using LLMs to summarize or analyze submissions (or sharing submission content with LLM services) violates confidentiality and is serious misconduct. Reviewers remain fully accountable for the accuracy of their reviews even if they used polishing tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: No minimum rejection quotas
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no fixed quotas requiring a minimum number of rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate each paper on its own merits without trying to meet a target rejection rate. Focus on the quality and contribution of the submission when forming recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling submissions from professional conference venues
rubrics_metrics.description: Four-page papers from professional conferences (e.g., ICIP or ICASSP) do not automatically violate dual-submission rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such submissions are not automatically considered dual submissions, but reviewers should still assess substantive value. Familiarize yourself with the policy and ask Area Chairs when in doubt.
